input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The shape check before Editor.edit_files tests only for os.PathLike and no longer wraps a plain str, so a string filename is passed on as an iterable and consumed character by character when building the editor command.
- failure path: click.edit(filename="notes.txt") launches the editor with the nine single-character files n, o, t, e, s, ., t, x, t instead of notes.txt; saving creates stray files in the working directory and the intended file is never opened.

Reviewer finding
- description: The check was changed from `isinstance(filename, str)` to `isinstance(filename, os.PathLike)`, so plain `str` is no longer wrapped in a tuple. Strings are not instances of os.PathLike.
- rationale: Trigger: `click.edit(filename="foo.txt")`. The string is passed unwrapped to edit_files, which iterates it character by character and tries to open each character as a separate file. The editor is launched with wrong arguments. This breaks the previously working common case.
critique: The finding identifies the same faulty operation: the isinstance check now tests only os.PathLike, so a plain str is not wrapped. It also gives the same failure mechanism, where edit_files iterates the string character by character and the editor opens per-character files. Both describe the click.edit(filename="...") trigger.
